only_in_confusable: [untitled BTM module] These genes converge on integrin-based adhesion and the cytoskeletal signalling that lets cells grip and respond to their extracellular matrix, with a supporting cast of metabolic and gene-regulatory proteins. Talin links activated integrin tails to actin, integrin-linked kinase couples the adhesion complex to downstream survival and contractility signalling, and a Rho GDP-dissociation inhibitor restrains Rho-family GTPases so that actin remodelling is switched rather than constant; a microtubule-associated protein and the SNARE-recycling factor alpha-SNAP tie the same events to cytoskeletal turnover and membrane fusion.

[untitled BTM module] These genes sketch a morphogen-driven programme that patterns mesenchymal tissue and steers progenitors toward bone, cartilage, skin and blood-supporting fates. BMP signalling sits at its centre: SMAD1 carries the receptor signal to the nucleus, ZNF521 acts as a nuclear cofactor tuning that output in skeletal and haematopoietic progenitors, while secreted GREM1 antagonises BMP ligands to keep niches permissive, and INHBA contributes an activin/TGF-beta arm through its own receptor-SMAD route.

[untitled BTM module] This grouping centres on TGF-β/BMP superfamily signalling and its downstream control of cell fate and growth arrest. BMP4 and the activin-like receptor ACVR1C transmit ligand binding into Smad-dependent transcription, with the repulsive guidance molecule RGMA acting as a BMP co-receptor, while CDKN2B encodes the p15 cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor that enforces the cytostatic response to these ligands in epithelial and haematopoietic cells.
